description: Where there is more to discover our Rocket will be there!
summary:
We developed RocketPulse, a hybrid online and offline Astronaut Health Monitoring and Clinical Decision Support System built with Next.js, FastAPI, and Supabase. It captures continuous physiological telemetry, medical imaging, and cabin environmental data across twelve clinical domains and seven role-based dashboards.

RocketPulse addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge by monitoring all Five Hazards of Human Spaceflight, specifically overcoming deep-space communication latency. It runs clinical triage and alert validation autonomously offline at the edge during network blackouts, automatically syncing updates with ground control whenever connectivity is available.

This system is critical for long-duration lunar and Martian missions where medical evacuation to Earth is impossible. By translating complex biomedical data into proactive, verified clinical decision support, RocketPulse ensures early detection of health risks and safeguards crew survival.
details:
The Autonomous Deep Space Astronaut Health Monitoring System is an offline first clinical decision support and data management platform engineered for deep space exploration missions facing high latency and communication blackouts. The architecture operates on an authoritative local first pipeline where telemetry from physiological monitors, environmental sensors, and manual crew inputs are validated locally via FastAPI and Pydantic, immediately committed to an onboard encrypted SQLite database, and processed through a versioned Python rules engine before any network transmission occurs. When orbital passes or ground communication windows open, a durable, append only sync queue transmits cryptographically hashed data packets to a Supabase PostgreSQL cloud instance with guaranteed idempotence, completely avoiding data loss or duplicate alerts. The platform feeds seven role specific dashboards, including Mission Medical Command, Individual Astronaut Health, Clinical Examinations, Radiation & Environment, Laboratory & Immune Health, Crew Self Assessment, and Ground Medical Review, enabling synchronized oversight between onboard crew members and Earth based flight surgeons across 12 distinct health and environmental domains.

The project addresses the five primary hazards of human spaceflight, which are radiation, isolation, distance from Earth, hostile environments, and altered gravity, by providing medical self sufficiency without reliance on continuous ground guidance. Built using React and TypeScript on the frontend alongside Python, FastAPI, SQLite, and Supabase PostgreSQL with Row Level Security, the software maintains complete traceability and auditability for longitudinal health data. It innovates through context aware analytics and strict clinical gating, differentiating expected physiological spikes like high heart rates during exercise from abnormal distress, and segregating experimental research metrics from approved clinical workflows. Critical safeguards strictly prohibit autonomous diagnosing, prescribing, or vehicle actuation, ensuring that human clinicians remain at the center of every medical decision. Every record enforces explicit quality and data provenance flags, isolating sensitive behavioral check ins and tagging all synthetic data to prevent misidentification, thereby establishing a deterministic, reproducible testing environment for deep space operational medicine.
